outcome: Since 26 January 2024 a Lean 4 (Mathlib) disproof of the constant-1 form has been posted (repository dated 3 September 2026, by Tom Adamczewski, crediting a pre-release GPT-6 Astra run in an Epoch AI evaluation); as of the latest sources read (13 October 2026) no mathematician outside the project had reviewed it, and the tracker labels it 'Candidate (review pending)'. Before that, the only in-window events were a restricted-class partial result (Jatar and Ng, 27 August 2026, which still calls the problem unsolved), dual-conjecture analogues, and a negative AlphaEvolve search (November 2025).
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone. (1) For every complex polynomial f of degree d >= 2 (the statement quantifies over all such f and all degrees). (2) For every complex number z. (3) Whether there exists a critical point c of f (f'(c) = 0, with c allowed to depend on f and z) such that |f(z) - f(c)| <= |f'(z)| * |z - c|. (4) With the constant exactly 1. The bullet is phrased as a question ('is there a critical point ...'), and the universal reading (every f and every z admits such a c) is the conjecture it names. The bullet does not itself ask about the sharp constant (d-1)/d, the best constant between 1 and 4, or the dual inequality; those are different questions that share the name and are discussed in the Wikipedia article and the literature, not in the bullet.

events.what_happened: Tom Adamczewski posted a GitHub repository (tadamcz/mean-value-problem), titled 'Lean 4 disproof of Smale's mean value conjecture (K = 1), found by GPT-6 Astra'. Its README says the conjecture with K = 1 is false and that the witness was 'found autonomously by a pre-release version of GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI)' in an evaluation run by Epoch AI, which the README names wikipedia-vega-1000usd and describes as running over the open statements of Formal Conjectures' Wikipedia collection. A VibeMathed tracker entry lists it as Disproved, status 'Candidate (review pending)', verification 'Lean-verified', with 'Solved 2026-09-03', submitted 4 Sep 2026 and approved for listing 5 Sep 2026. MathWorld (page updated 2 Oct 2026) cites it as Adamczewski (2026) and calls it a 'proposed counterexample'. The Wikipedia article 'Mean value problem' now carries the short description 'Mathematical problem in complex analysis, disproved in 2026' (last edited 13 Sep 2026), while its body still presents the K = 1 case as open.
events.revisions: Four commits visible on the repository, all by the author: 3 Sep 2026 (two: 'Package the GPT-6 Astra resolution ... for Palomar' and 'Report cost at GPT-6 Astra's actual prices and working time'), 6 Sep 2026 ('Update authorship note at top of README'), 17 Sep 2026 ('Remove references to Palomar from the README'). The run used Lean v4.27.0; the README later targets Lean v4.28.0 / Mathlib v4.28.0. No arXiv version or journal version found.
events.delivers: Claims that the constant-1 inequality fails for some normalised polynomial. Witness: a complex polynomial p of degree at least 2 with p(0) = 0 and p'(0) = 1 such that |p(c)/c| > 1 at every critical point c, so at z = 0 no critical point satisfies the inequality. In the Lean file (Challenge.lean, with the proof in an imported module) this is the negation of the universal statement that every polynomial of degree >= 2 and every z admit a critical point c with ||p(z) - p(c)|| / ||z - c|| <= ||p'(z)||. Restrictions: one witness, at z = 0, of degree the README calls 'very large, unspecified' and does not write out. It refutes the universal constant-1 claim as stated and nothing finer.
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet's universal claim remains open if the Lean statement faithfully encodes the bullet and the proof is sound; both are unverified by anyone outside the project (see doubts). Not addressed: the value of the best constant in any particular degree; the sharp (d-1)/d form, which is a different question; whether the witness is schlicht (relevant to the Jatar and Ng event); and whether the witness degree lies in any range where earlier numerical checks would have caught it.

checked_by.what_they_did: The README says Comparator checks that the challenge statement and the compared theorem coincide and that only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice are used. I did not run it; I read the README's description.

events.time_since_posted: about six weeks as of 13 Oct 2026

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib, checked by Comparator according to the repository

events.directly_checkable: Not by hand from the record. The witness is not written out: AllBadWitness (a definition in the Lean module) is satisfied by a polynomial obtained by polynomial approximation of a model function plus a perturbation family, indexed by an n 'sufficiently large'. No coefficients are given. The check is the Lean development, which I did not compile.
events.doubts: (1) Single source. Only the author's repository, a tracker and MathWorld's citation of it; no arXiv write-up, journal submission, or expert commentary found through 13 Oct 2026. VibeMathed says: 'No independent mathematician has checked this yet.' and 'Candidate rather than resolved because, two days after the run, no mathematician outside it has read the proof.' and 'The proof account was machine-generated and is unaudited.' MathWorld says independent review had not been reported as of 7 Sep 2026. (2) Authorship. The README says 'No human saw or steered the proof search.' It also says the entire repository was 'machine-written by AI assistants at the direction of Tom Adamczewski' (the assistants are not named). (3) Non-explicit witness with degree stated only as 'very large, unspecified'. (4) Statement fidelity, which is the human question the Lean check does not settle. Challenge.lean's theorem binds an extra real variable K (written as 'forall (K : R)') that the conclusion never uses. I judge this logically harmless because the reals are inhabited, but a reader should look. The inequality uses Lean's division convention (x/0 = 0); I checked by hand that it agrees with the multiplicative form |f(z)-f(c)| <= |f'(z)||z-c| in both the z = c and z != c cases, but that is my reading. The upstream Formal Conjectures entry the file says it follows was not found. (5) Relationship. Adamczewski's Epoch AI page bio says 'Tom Adamczewski started Epoch AI's benchmark engineering team', and the run is described as Epoch's. Epoch's public results repository (19 commits) lists runs named oeis-..., bloom68-... and erdos-... but not wikipedia-vega-1000usd, so the run name is not confirmed from Epoch's side as far as I could read. (6) Cost. The README reports $265 'at GPT-6 Astra's standard rates' and a commit reports that figure was changed to 'actual prices'. Epoch's results README says that because no prices had been published, the harness metered GPT-6 Astra spend at GPT-5.6 Sol's prices. The two bases are not reconciled. (7) A Chinese-language AI4Math tracker record (PR #41, merged 1 Oct 2026) says the original construction was later mathematically checked and generalised by Adamczewski, Bohmler and Marczinzik. The only Bohmler and Marczinzik paper I found with Adamczewski is a counterexample to Kothe's conjecture (arXiv 2609.07996), and I found no link to Smale's problem, so I treat that claim as unverified and probably a mix-up. (8) The model name is the authors' own; they call it a pre-release version. I could not verify any public release, and I do not date it.
events.direction: Against. The claim is that the constant-1 inequality is false: a witness at z = 0 violates it at every critical point. The bullet's universal reading predicts the opposite answer ('yes, there is always such a c'), so the claim cuts against the conjecture as worded. Consequence for the sharp form (my inference, not stated in the sources): a degree-d witness with min |p(c)/c| > 1 would also contradict the sharp bound M_d = (d-1)/d at that degree, because (d-1)/d < 1. The bullet does not ask about the sharp form.
events.object: A complex polynomial p of degree d >= 2 (degree 'very large, unspecified' per the README and not written out), normalised so that p(0) = 0 and p'(0) = 1, with |p(c)/c| > 1 at every critical point c. So at z = 0 no critical point satisfies the constant-1 inequality. Non-constructive: it is built in Lean from a model function, a polynomial approximation of that model, and a perturbation family anchored at z0, with existence proved as exists_allBadWitness. Coefficients are not given anywhere in the sources I read.
people: Tom Adamczewski (repository author; the README says the repository was machine-written at their direction; Epoch AI's own page describes them as starting Epoch's benchmark engineering team)

events.what_happened: Preprint 'Smale's Mean Value Conjecture and its Dual Conjecture for Complex Polynomials' by Aneesh Jatar and Tuen Wai Ng (Hong Kong). Its introduction says the conjecture 'is still unsolved' and that it was 'studied by the AI tool AlphaEvolve in Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner's problem list' without finding a counterexample. Results: (i) restricting to Schlicht normalised polynomials, the bound 1 becomes asymptotically valid as the degree tends to infinity when the leading coefficient decays slowly enough; (ii) an improved Markov-type inequality for maximal univalent lemniscates, for the dual conjecture; (iii) an improved unconditional lower bound (d - 1/2)^(1/d) / d^2 for the dual, improving Dubinin's 1/d^2.
events.revisions: v1 only, submitted 27 Aug 2026, 40 pages (arXiv listing).
events.delivers: Result (i) is a restricted-class, asymptotic statement about the constant-1 inequality: for Schlicht normalised polynomials with slowly decaying leading coefficient, the bound 1 holds asymptotically as d grows. Results (ii) and (iii) concern the dual lower-bound conjecture, a different question. Result (i) does not establish the universal claim for all polynomials and all z, and says nothing for fixed small degree.
events.remains: The universal constant-1 claim for all polynomials of degree at least 2 and all z; the non-Schlicht case; the non-asymptotic (fixed-degree) case.
events.time_since_posted: about seven weeks as of 13 Oct 2026
events.doubts: Predates the 3 Sep 2026 disproof claim, so its 'still unsolved' sentence does not address it. Whether the disproof witness is Schlicht, and what its leading coefficient looks like, is not stated in the disproof repository, so the two cannot be compared. If the witness were Schlicht with a suitably slowly decaying leading coefficient at large degree, result (i) would conflict with it; the sources do not settle this. I read only the first 100,000 characters of the HTML; the acknowledgements and any AI-use disclosure were not read.
events.direction: For the restricted Schlicht asymptotic class, consistent with the constant-1 inequality (a partial result in the direction the conjecture predicts). The paper's own status sentence says the conjecture is unsolved.

events.what_happened: Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner, 'Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale' (arXiv 2511.02864). Problem 6.23 is Smale's problem, stated with C_Smale(n), the least constant such that for any polynomial f of degree n and any z with f'(z) != 0 there is a critical point xi with |f(z) - f(xi)| / |z - xi| <= C_Smale(n) |f'(z)|. The paper cites Smale's bounds 1 - 1/n <= C(n) <= 4, and Smale's conjecture that C(n) = 1 - 1/n. The AlphaEvolve experiment matched the best known lower bound, using the extremal polynomial z^n - nz, and found other constructions with similar scores. The paper reports that it 'did not manage to find a counterexample' and did not improve the bounds.
events.revisions: v1 submitted 3 Nov 2025; v3 last revised 22 Dec 2025 (arXiv listing). Version 2 not separately checked.
events.delivers: Nothing new on the bullet. It is a negative computational search: AlphaEvolve reproduced the known lower bound and found no counterexample to the constant-1 claim. The degrees searched are not stated in the portion I read; the example constructions shown include degree 12 (z^12 - 12z and a second degree-12 polynomial).
events.remains: All of problem_asks; the search cannot settle a universal claim.
events.time_since_posted: about eleven months as of 13 Oct 2026
events.doubts: The quoted sentences ('AlphaEvolve matched the best known lower bound for C_Smale(n)' and 'did not manage to find a counterexample') came through a summarising fetch of the HTML, so their exact wording should be checked against the PDF. I read Problem 6.23 across the HTML range I could fetch; the paper's full text was longer and not all read.
events.direction: None. A negative search; it neither supports nor contradicts the constant-1 claim, and it says it found no counterexample.

systems.name: AlphaEvolve
systems.what_it_did: Evolutionary search over constructions, with an LLM proposing candidate programs and automated scoring (the paper's own description of AlphaEvolve). On Problem 6.23 it searched for constructions scoring against the lower bound. It rediscovered the known bound and found no counterexample and no improvement. This was a search that did not feed a result on the bullet, so it is recorded here, not weighed as a contribution.
systems.basis_quote: AlphaEvolve matched the best known lower bound for C_Smale(n)

events.what_happened: Quanyu Tang, 'Dual Smale's mean value conjecture for odd polynomials' (arXiv 2510.16875). Proves the dual conjecture for all odd polynomials with nonzero linear term: for normalised P (P(0) = 0, P'(0) = 1) of degree d >= 3 there is a critical point zeta with |P(zeta)/zeta| >= 1/d. The introduction says Smale's mean value conjecture 'has resisted proof despite extensive efforts by many leading mathematicians' and that 'the general case remains unresolved'.
events.delivers: A result on the dual lower-bound question for a restricted class (odd polynomials with nonzero linear term). It is the dual inequality, a different question, and it is restricted to odd polynomials. It is recorded as an analogue. It does not bear on the constant-1 upper inequality.
events.remains: The dual conjecture for even and general polynomials; the constant-1 bullet, which this result does not touch.
events.time_since_posted: about one year as of 13 Oct 2026
events.direction: Not against or for the bullet. It settles a dual lower-bound question on a restricted class.

disputes.summary: Status of the constant-1 claim is inconsistent across sources. The Wikipedia short description says 'disproved in 2026' (last edited 13 Sep 2026) while its body still describes K = 1 as open. MathWorld (updated 2 Oct 2026) calls the Adamczewski result a 'proposed counterexample'. The VibeMathed tracker says 'Candidate (review pending)' and 'No independent mathematician has checked this yet'. Jatar and Ng (27 Aug 2026, predating the claim) say the problem is unsolved.

The repository credits the Lean proof to GPT-6 Astra ('The Lean proof itself was written by GPT-6 Astra') and the search to no human ('No human saw or steered the proof search'), but also says the whole repository was 'machine-written by AI assistants at the direction of Tom Adamczewski' (unnamed assistants). The record does not pick between these; the later pass should read both.

Claimed full proofs of the conjecture from 2002 (Schmieder), 2017 (Wang, withdrawn) and 2022 (Ma and Ma, not refuted in the sources read) conflict with the 'still unsolved' status in the 2026 literature. Schmieder's claim is refuted in the Borcea critique (2003); Wang's was withdrawn by its author; Ma and Ma's has no visible engagement.

The disclosed cost basis differs: the README reports $265 at GPT-6 Astra's standard rates, while Epoch's results repository says the harness metered GPT-6 Astra at GPT-5.6 Sol's prices because no prices had been published.

An AI4Math tracker record (PR #41) says the original construction was later checked and generalised by Adamczewski, Bohmler and Marczinzik. I found that Bohmler and Marczinzik co-wrote a different paper with Adamczewski (a Kothe conjecture counterexample, arXiv 2609.07996) and no link to Smale's problem. Treat the claim as unverified and probably a mix-up.

summary: Found one in-window claim that bears directly on the bullet, and a long pre-window history. (1) On 3 Sep 2026 Tom Adamczewski posted a Lean 4 (Mathlib) disproof of the constant-1 inequality. The README credits the witness and the Lean proof to a pre-release GPT-6 Astra run in an Epoch AI evaluation, and says no human steered the proof search. I read the README, the challenge statement and the imported module through summarising fetches; I did not compile them or run Comparator. The Lean statement is the negation of the universal constant-1 claim; the witness is a normalised polynomial p (p(0)=0, p'(0)=1) of degree described only as 'very large, unspecified', with |p(c)/c| > 1 at every critical point, at z = 0. The witness is non-explicit. No mathematician review was found: the VibeMathed tracker says none has checked it, and MathWorld (updated 2 Oct 2026) reports no review as of 7 Sep 2026. Two parts of Wikipedia disagree: the short description says 'disproved in 2026' and the body still treats K = 1 as open. Close calls: (a) whether the disproof resolves the bullet depends on whether the Lean statement faithfully encodes it (an unused K binder; x/0 = 0 convention, which I judge harmless on my reading) and on accepting a single AI-generated, unreviewed proof; (b) my inference is that a degree-d witness would also contradict the sharp (d-1)/d form at that degree, although the bullet does not ask for it; (c) Jatar and Ng's restricted Schlicht asymptotic result (27 Aug 2026, predating the claim) would conflict with a Schlicht witness with slowly decaying leading coefficient at large degree; the sources do not say whether the witness is Schlicht. On AI involvement: the authors' own account (README) credits GPT-6 Astra with the Lean proof and the autonomous search, which is load-bearing and recorded in ai.systems. The same README says the whole repository was machine-written by unnamed 'AI assistants'; those are not recorded as systems. Epoch's public results repository, read, lists no run named wikipedia-vega-1000usd, though it does describe GPT-6 Astra as a pre-release model; the run name is therefore not confirmed from Epoch's side. Epoch's own page says Adamczewski started its benchmark engineering team. (2) AI search in the window: AlphaEvolve on Problem 6.23 (Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner, 3 Nov 2025) rediscovered the known lower bound and found no counterexample; it is a null search and recorded as such. (3) Partial and analogue results in the window: Jatar and Ng (Aug 2026, restricted asymptotic plus dual results); Tang (Oct 2025, dual, odd polynomials); Hinkkanen et al. (dual, degree 7, preprint March 2023, journal 2025); Dubinin (2024, Blaschke analogue). (4) Pre-window claims of proofs: Schmieder (2002), refuted per Borcea (2003); Wang (2017), withdrawn; Ma and Ma (2022), no visible engagement. Pre-window partial results: Smale (1981, constant 4), Tischler (1989, two special classes), Ng (2003, odd polynomials, constant 2), Marinov and Sendov (2007, numerical, n <= 10), Crane and Conte et al. (2007, constant bounds), plus dual and analogue papers recorded as discounted events. Dead ends: Tao's blog and Mathstodon (nothing found); a 'Bohmler and Marczinzik' claim in a tracker record (unverified, probably a mix-up); Watanabe's disproof of the 4-dimensional Smale conjecture (a different problem); and the Epoch FrontierMath Erdos paper, the Sra 'GPT, the Counterexample Machine' paper and the 'Endless Exam' paper, whose abstracts do not mention Smale (their bodies were not readable).
competing_reading: The strongest case against counting the disproof is that it is one unreviewed claim: the only proof is the author's own AI-generated Lean development, the Lean statement's fidelity to the bullet has not been checked by a human, the witness is non-explicit with no stated degree, and the Wikipedia body and the Aug 2026 Jatar and Ng paper still describe the problem as open. On that reading the bullet stays open, the disproof is a candidate pending review, and it should not be treated as settling the problem until a complex-analysis specialist has checked the statement and the construction. The contrary reading, that the disproof is a formal refutation of the universal claim as stated, rests on the Lean development compiling with only standard axioms and the statement matching the bullet, which the record shows only by the author's own account.
what_would_settle_it: (i) A human reading of Challenge.lean against Smale's 1981 statement and the Wikipedia wording, including whether the unused real K binder and the x/0 convention change the statement. (ii) A successful lake build and Comparator run on the repository at its stated toolchain, by someone other than the author. (iii) A mathematician's account of the witness's construction (the approximation and perturbation steps) and of its degree, and whether that degree is above the range of earlier numerical checks. (iv) An arXiv write-up or journal submission, and any response from complex analysts. (v) Epoch's own record of the wikipedia-vega-1000usd run (its results, the identity of the pre-release model, and the cost basis). (vi) Whether the Wikipedia body text is updated to match its short description. (vii) Whether the witness is Schlicht, and if so with what leading coefficient, to settle its relation to Jatar and Ng's asymptotic result.

event.what_happened: Tom Adamczewski posted a GitHub repository (tadamcz/mean-value-problem), titled 'Lean 4 disproof of Smale's mean value conjecture (K = 1), found by GPT-6 Astra'. Its README says the conjecture with K = 1 is false and that the witness was 'found autonomously by a pre-release version of GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI)' in an evaluation run by Epoch AI, which the README names wikipedia-vega-1000usd and describes as running over the open statements of Formal Conjectures' Wikipedia collection. A VibeMathed tracker entry lists it as Disproved, status 'Candidate (review pending)', verification 'Lean-verified', with 'Solved 2026-09-03', submitted 4 Sep 2026 and approved for listing 5 Sep 2026. MathWorld (page updated 2 Oct 2026) cites it as Adamczewski (2026) and calls it a 'proposed counterexample'. The Wikipedia article 'Mean value problem' now carries the short description 'Mathematical problem in complex analysis, disproved in 2026' (last edited 13 Sep 2026), while its body still presents the K = 1 case as open.
event.revisions: Four commits visible on the repository, all by the author: 3 Sep 2026 (two: 'Package the GPT-6 Astra resolution ... for Palomar' and 'Report cost at GPT-6 Astra's actual prices and working time'), 6 Sep 2026 ('Update authorship note at top of README'), 17 Sep 2026 ('Remove references to Palomar from the README'). The run used Lean v4.27.0; the README later targets Lean v4.28.0 / Mathlib v4.28.0. No arXiv version or journal version found.
event.delivers: Claims that the constant-1 inequality fails for some normalised polynomial. Witness: a complex polynomial p of degree at least 2 with p(0) = 0 and p'(0) = 1 such that |p(c)/c| > 1 at every critical point c, so at z = 0 no critical point satisfies the inequality. In the Lean file (Challenge.lean, with the proof in an imported module) this is the negation of the universal statement that every polynomial of degree >= 2 and every z admit a critical point c with ||p(z) - p(c)|| / ||z - c|| <= ||p'(z)||. Restrictions: one witness, at z = 0, of degree the README calls 'very large, unspecified' and does not write out. It refutes the universal constant-1 claim as stated and nothing finer.
event.remains: Nothing of the bullet's universal claim remains open if the Lean statement faithfully encodes the bullet and the proof is sound; both are unverified by anyone outside the project (see doubts). Not addressed: the value of the best constant in any particular degree; the sharp (d-1)/d form, which is a different question; whether the witness is schlicht (relevant to the Jatar and Ng event); and whether the witness degree lies in any range where earlier numerical checks would have caught it.

checked_by.who: Comparator (Lean verification tool), run by the repository's own script
checked_by.what_they_did: The README says Comparator checks that the challenge statement and the compared theorem coincide and that only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice are used. I did not run it; I read the README's description.

event.time_since_posted: about six weeks as of 13 Oct 2026

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib, checked by Comparator according to the repository

event.directly_checkable: Not by hand from the record. The witness is not written out: AllBadWitness (a definition in the Lean module) is satisfied by a polynomial obtained by polynomial approximation of a model function plus a perturbation family, indexed by an n 'sufficiently large'. No coefficients are given. The check is the Lean development, which I did not compile.
event.doubts: (1) Single source. Only the author's repository, a tracker and MathWorld's citation of it; no arXiv write-up, journal submission, or expert commentary found through 13 Oct 2026. VibeMathed says: 'No independent mathematician has checked this yet.' and 'Candidate rather than resolved because, two days after the run, no mathematician outside it has read the proof.' and 'The proof account was machine-generated and is unaudited.' MathWorld says independent review had not been reported as of 7 Sep 2026. (2) Authorship. The README says 'No human saw or steered the proof search.' It also says the entire repository was 'machine-written by AI assistants at the direction of Tom Adamczewski' (the assistants are not named). (3) Non-explicit witness with degree stated only as 'very large, unspecified'. (4) Statement fidelity, which is the human question the Lean check does not settle. Challenge.lean's theorem binds an extra real variable K (written as 'forall (K : R)') that the conclusion never uses. I judge this logically harmless because the reals are inhabited, but a reader should look. The inequality uses Lean's division convention (x/0 = 0); I checked by hand that it agrees with the multiplicative form |f(z)-f(c)| <= |f'(z)||z-c| in both the z = c and z != c cases, but that is my reading. The upstream Formal Conjectures entry the file says it follows was not found. (5) Relationship. Adamczewski's Epoch AI page bio says 'Tom Adamczewski started Epoch AI's benchmark engineering team', and the run is described as Epoch's. Epoch's public results repository (19 commits) lists runs named oeis-..., bloom68-... and erdos-... but not wikipedia-vega-1000usd, so the run name is not confirmed from Epoch's side as far as I could read. (6) Cost. The README reports $265 'at GPT-6 Astra's standard rates' and a commit reports that figure was changed to 'actual prices'. Epoch's results README says that because no prices had been published, the harness metered GPT-6 Astra spend at GPT-5.6 Sol's prices. The two bases are not reconciled. (7) A Chinese-language AI4Math tracker record (PR #41, merged 1 Oct 2026) says the original construction was later mathematically checked and generalised by Adamczewski, Bohmler and Marczinzik. The only Bohmler and Marczinzik paper I found with Adamczewski is a counterexample to Kothe's conjecture (arXiv 2609.07996), and I found no link to Smale's problem, so I treat that claim as unverified and probably a mix-up. (8) The model name is the authors' own; they call it a pre-release version. I could not verify any public release, and I do not date it.
event.direction: Against. The claim is that the constant-1 inequality is false: a witness at z = 0 violates it at every critical point. The bullet's universal reading predicts the opposite answer ('yes, there is always such a c'), so the claim cuts against the conjecture as worded. Consequence for the sharp form (my inference, not stated in the sources): a degree-d witness with min |p(c)/c| > 1 would also contradict the sharp bound M_d = (d-1)/d at that degree, because (d-1)/d < 1. The bullet does not ask about the sharp form.
event.object: A complex polynomial p of degree d >= 2 (degree 'very large, unspecified' per the README and not written out), normalised so that p(0) = 0 and p'(0) = 1, with |p(c)/c| > 1 at every critical point c. So at z = 0 no critical point satisfies the constant-1 inequality. Non-constructive: it is built in Lean from a model function, a polynomial approximation of that model, and a perturbation family anchored at z0, with existence proved as exists_allBadWitness. Coefficients are not given anywhere in the sources I read.

judgement.why: The statement asks one universal question at constant 1. A valid counterexample therefore answers all of it, so the Adamczewski/GPT-6 Astra disproof is scope whole. It is unreviewed: the only check is a Lean/Comparator build (F7), and the witness is non-explicit, so it is not checkable. I rated it doubtful rather than not_credible. No error has been identified and the author is an established figure, but the evidence is single-source, the Epoch run is unconfirmed, nobody has checked statement fidelity, and the repository was machine-written. The README says the witness was found autonomously by GPT-6 Astra, so its AI role is generated. Jatar and Ng's Schlicht asymptotic result is a restricted case, and that call was close: it is asymptotic rather than exact. AlphaEvolve's negative search delivered nothing, and its own quote shows only that it reproduced a known bound, so it is none. Dual, Blaschke, C*-algebra, Tischler-strong-form and constant-2 odd-polynomial results are variants. Constant bounds (Smale's 4, Crane, Conte et al., Beardon et al.) are bounds on the constant and leave the question open. Pre-window claimed proofs are knocked_down (Wang withdrawn; Schmieder refuted by Borcea), and Ma and Ma's is not_credible. Dubinin 2024 is year-only, so its after_snapshot is null.
judgement.doubts: The disproof's correctness rests entirely on an unreviewed machine-generated Lean development. Nobody has independently checked that Challenge.lean encodes the bullet: the unused K binder and the x/0 convention were judged harmless only by the researcher. The relation between the witness and Jatar and Ng's Schlicht result is unresolved. Marinov and Sendov's journal verification is treated as digested from secondary reports only.
